items.title: 60322_John Bubbles oral history interview
items.q: the manager's name was John Gibson, colored man who owns the theater and he decided he would take us in

ctx.x: We go on to New York. I get to New York, now I've got to scout out the music. I didn't have no music now, got to scout out dancing shoes and costumes to work in and I got to get a date. So I get a date in a

colored theater that we played in in Philadelphia called the Standard Theater, the manager's name was John Gibson, colored man who owns the theater and he decided he would take us in because he knew we would act. See all of us had played there before, all four of us had played there before in an act. But I'm coming back this time with just Buck and I and he booked us. He charged us -- to borrow money now you had to pay 10% of whatever you borrowed. He couldn't advance on salary less than 10%. Okay. So I borrowed…

We opened up, good success, I got to get another booking. So I booked in Newark. So in Newark he enjoined us in getting on the stage -- enjoined, do you understand me?
